name: run.vertfinder/vertfinder
title: Vertfinder
description: Find runnable hills near you, plan hilly routes, and match a race's climbs to local hills.

tools.name: find_climbs
tools.description:
Find real hills near a location, nearest first (or biggest first with sort_by: gain).
Coverage: the United Kingdom, Ireland, France, Switzerland, Austria, Berlin and Brandenburg, California, Oregon, Washington,
British Columbia, Colorado, New York, New Jersey, Massachusetts, the Chicago area, the Tokyo area, Sydney and Cape Town; elsewhere has no climbs.
Only climbs within max_distance_km (default 10) are returned; if there are too few, call again with a larger radius.
Climbs are OpenStreetMap roads and trails (footpaths, tracks, bridleways, steps) with elevation from 1 arc-second terrain data.
Use for hill sprints, hill repeats or hilly runs: a long climb can be used for shorter reps.
For planning a hilly run or matching a race's climbing, use sort_by: gain and a wider max_distance_km, then pass climbs to plan_route.
Each result links to walking directions to the bottom (googleMapsUrl) and to the climb on the vertfinder map (vertfinderUrl);
show each climb to the person as a markdown link to its vertfinderUrl, not as a wayId.
Each result has gap_dist_m, its flat-equivalent length from an approximation of Strava's GAP curve. Give a pace (mm:ss per km or mile)
to get est_ascent_seconds, an estimate of one rep up the climb; with min_minutes/max_minutes it only returns climbs whose ascent fits that range,
e.g. for 3, 6 or 10 minute hill reps. pace_mode gap (default) treats the pace as flat-equivalent effort; pace treats it as the actual uphill pace.

location.description: Postcode, town or place name, searched worldwide: add a region or country (e.g. "Richmond, North Yorkshire, UK") and check the returned location. Required unless lat and lon are given.

lat.description: latitude; with lon, takes precedence over location

lon.description: longitude; with lat, takes precedence over location

min_length_m.description: minimum climb length in metres (at least 200 unless steps is set)

pavement.description: only road climbs mapped with a pavement along their whole length; many roads lack pavement data in OpenStreetMap, so this also drops climbs whose pavement is unknown

steps.description: only trail climbs that include at least one flight of steps; also includes staircases shorter than 200 m

max_distance_km.description: only return climbs within this many km, at least 0.1 (default 10)

min_gain_m.description: minimum approximate climb gain in metres (default 0)

sort_by.description: distance (nearest first, default) or gain (biggest climbs in the radius first; use for planning hilly routes)

pace.description: running pace as mm:ss per pace_unit, e.g. 6:00; enables est_ascent_seconds and the minutes filters

pace_mode.description: gap (default: pace is flat-equivalent effort, adjusted for gradient) or pace (actual uphill pace)

min_minutes.description: only climbs whose estimated ascent takes at least this many minutes; needs pace

max_minutes.description: only climbs whose estimated ascent takes at most this many minutes; needs pace

tools.name: get_climb
tools.description:
Get details of one climb by wayId (from find_climbs): length, average and maximum gradient,
bottom and top coordinates, links, and a gradient profile in 100 m sections from the bottom.

tools.name: get_race
tools.description:
Get the climbing analysis of a race (id from list_races or a start_race_upload curl upload): distance, total gain, gain per distance (gainPct),
the average and steepest 100 m gradient of its climbs of 25 m gain or more, and every rise of 10 m gain or more. Groups put the
rises into fixed gain bands (label "10-25", "25-50", "50-100", "100-250", "250-500", "500-1000" or "1000+", with bandMinM and
bandMaxM, null for the top band), each with its count, smallest and biggest rise, total gain and median rise.
Race ids expire and only work for the person who uploaded them. Then call match_race_climbs.

race_id.description: the race id returned by uploading the GPX

tools.name: list_races
tools.description:
List the person's race GPX files uploaded to vertfinder, newest first, with id, name, distance and total gain.
Use it after the person uploads a GPX through a start_race_upload link or the upload button in the vertfinder app,
then pass the id to get_race or match_race_climbs. Races expire after expiresAt.

tools.name: match_race_climbs
tools.description:
Find local hills to train on for a race's climbing (race_id from get_race).
For each gain band of 25 m or more in the race, returns up to 5 climbs within max_km (default 25, 1-250). With mode
"match", they are the nearest climbs similar enough to the band's median rise (score 60-100 for similarity of gain,
average gradient and steepest 100 m), widening 10, 25 then 100 km up to max_km, with repeats 1; an empty list means
nothing similar within max_km. With allow_repeats, such bands instead get mode "repeat": the biggest climbs at a
similar gradient, with repeats saying how many climbs of each match the median rise; an empty list then means no hill
within max_km. Near-duplicates are removed. Pass wayIds to get_climb for
details or to plan_route for a route.

race_id.description: the race id returned by uploading the GPX

location.description: Postcode, town or place name, searched worldwide: add a region or country (e.g. "Richmond, North Yorkshire, UK") and check the returned location. Required unless lat and lon are given.

lat.description: latitude; with lon, takes precedence over location

lon.description: longitude; with lat, takes precedence over location

max_km.description: furthest distance to search in km, 1-250 (default 25)

allow_repeats.description: when a band has no similar climb, suggest smaller hills to repeat instead (default false)

tools.name: plan_route
tools.description:
Route a run on foot from a start point through ordered stops, by default back to the start.
Stops are climbs from find_climbs (way_id, run bottom to top; repeats runs extra reps back down and up) or lat/lon points.
Returns distance, ascent and descent, gain and loss for each km, an elevation profile every 100 m,
a GPX download link (gpxUrl) and a map link (mapUrl), and a vertfinderUrl for each climb on the route. Route links expire at expiresAt.
To hit a target such as 750 m ascent over 30 km: find big climbs with find_climbs sort_by: gain,
order stops so the climbing falls where the target profile needs it, add repeats for extra gain,
then compare gainPerKm with the target and adjust stops.
Each account can plan only a few routes a day, so settle the stops before calling, and keep them within about 100 km.

location.description: start: postcode, town or place name, searched worldwide: add a region or country (e.g. "Richmond, North Yorkshire, UK") and check the returned location. Required unless lat and lon are given.

lat.description: start latitude; with lon, takes precedence over location

lon.description: start longitude; with lat, takes precedence over location

way_id.description: a wayId from find_climbs; routed bottom to top

repeats.description: times to run the climb, 1-10 (default 1); extra reps go back to the bottom and up again

lat.description: latitude of a point to pass through (with lon, instead of way_id)

lon.description: longitude of a point to pass through (with lat, instead of way_id)

return_to_start.description: finish back at the start (default true)

tools.name: start_race_upload
tools.description:
Get a single-use link for uploading a race GPX to vertfinder, which analyses it.
Never send a GPX's contents through this conversation or analyse it yourself. If you can run shell commands with internet
access, run the returned curl command with the file's path; it responds with the race id. Otherwise give the person uploadUrl
as a link: it opens an upload page where they choose the file. When they say it's done, call list_races and use the newest race.
The link works once and expires at expiresAt (30 minutes).
